definition: in a brief and clearly expressed manner
memoryTip: Succinct = cinched tight like a belt—short and clear.
correctPassage: She explained the method succinctly in under two minutes.
wrongPassages: He spoke so succinctly that the lecture ran three hours past the scheduled end.
The report was written succinctly, filling twelve appendices with digressions.
She answered succinctly by retelling the same story with more detail each time.

definition: showing great attention to correct detail or form
memoryTip: Punctual about points—picky about every detail of etiquette.
correctPassage: A punctilious editor catches inconsistencies others miss.
wrongPassages: His punctilious approach skipped half the checklist and ignored the dress code.
She was too punctilious to notice that the form had the wrong date and signature.
The punctilious filing system tossed every document into a single unmarked bin.

correctPassage: The eldritch atmosphere of the story unsettled even adult readers.
wrongPassages: The eldritch kitchen felt warm and ordinary after a long day of errands.
Neighbors called the eldritch block party cheerful, familiar, and completely normal.
She preferred eldritch lighting that made every corner bright and inviting.

memoryTip: Ob-fus-cate: cloud over—deliberately make it hard to understand.
correctPassage: Legal jargon can obfuscate rather than clarify responsibility.
wrongPassages: The diagram was redesigned to obfuscate the process so beginners could follow it.
Teachers asked students to obfuscate their main claim in one clear sentence.
The FAQ was rewritten to obfuscate common questions with plain-language answers.

memoryTip: Clear joints of speech—express ideas smoothly and clearly.
correctPassage: Few candidates could articulate a clear plan for the district.
wrongPassages: He could only articulate in broken fragments that left listeners more confused.
She refused to articulate any position, sitting silent through the entire debate.
His attempt to articulate collapsed into mumbled half-sentences no one could parse.
